findings: At 88.9 percent of the all-W4 byte cost, the mixed assignment is 47.6 percent below all-W3 error and 22.9 percent above all-W4 error on one held-out sequence.
Calibration per-expert errors underestimate held-out error by roughly an order of magnitude because calibration quantizes one expert at a time while the held-out controls quantize all 288 at once.
W2 is unusable at scale here: all-W2 held-out error is 0.1564 versus 0.0238 for all-W4.

method.budget_rule: midpoint of the all-W3 and all-W4 per-expert byte costs
method.candidates: group-32 symmetric round-to-nearest at 4, 3, and 2 bits
method.selection: start every expert at 2 bits and apply the largest error reduction per marginal byte that fits the budget

non_claims: Layer 0 only; the other 47 layers, PLE, and end-to-end logits are not measured.
One calibration and one held-out sequence, not the recipe's 256 and 64.
Candidates are RTN, not GPTQ or the stock RCO optimizer.
No serving path, throughput, VRAM figure, or full-model artifact exists for this assignment.
scope: Layer-scope quantization-aware RCO measurement on the real 288-expert own-Coder layer 0
